## Repository boundaries {#sec-repository-layout}

```text
Project.toml                 active-root dependencies and bundled [sources]
src/PMFGLM.jl                public package facade
src/configuration.jl         TOML validation and environment mapping
src/provenance.jl            fingerprints, metadata, isolated run process
src/production/runner.jl     extracted full coupled production driver
lib/MHDKernels/              GLM MHD, PMF ICs, photon response, source coupling
lib/PoissonKernels/          periodic gravity, particle mesh, transforms, spectra
lib/ChemistryKernels/        primordial chemistry/recombination sources
lib/EmissionKernels/         thermal/cooling coefficients
scripts/                    bootstrap, launch, IC/suite generation, validation, benchmark
environments/{metal,cuda}/   optional GPU active roots with local source mappings
examples/                   small checks and editable research TOML
tools/reference/            independent linear/hierarchy science tools
tools/analysis/             history, spectrum, PDF, comparison analysis
test/                       Julia regressions and Python reference/analysis tests
provenance/                 source-extraction record
docs/                       this Quarto book and supplied test evidence
```

The extracted production driver is large because it retains the complete
coupled update, initialization choices, diagnostics, and restart contract.
The facade makes that driver reproducible without requiring users to edit it.
This is a single-node package, not Vespa's AMR/multi-code orchestration framework.

## Public facade {#sec-api-map}

| Entry point | Contract |
|---|---|
| `RunConfig(settings)` | Validate a configuration dictionary |
| `load_config(path)` | Read and validate a TOML experiment |
| `validate_config(config)` | Check named keys and structural constraints |
| `run_environment(config; output_dir)` | Resolve named and low-level solver options |
| `run_simulation(config; output_dir, dry_run=false)` | Launch a fresh process with metadata and controlled environment |
| `source_fingerprint()` | Hash implementation sources/declarations independently of checkout location |
| `backend`, `allocate_state`, `step!`, `evolve!`, `compute_dt` | Selected MHD operations |
| `init_pmf_batchelor!`, `pmf_batchelor_field` | PMF initialization |
| `fields_to_host`, `max_divb` | Host inspection and magnetic-divergence diagnostic |

{{< src "src/PMFGLM.jl" "export RunConfig" >}}

The exported library modules expose additional APIs with Julia docstrings.
Use Julia help, for example `?PMFGLM.MHDKernels.allocate_state`. The local
source links in this book are checked snapshots, not a claim that an automatic
Documenter-generated API reference exists.

## Process and data flow {#sec-run-flow}

1. The CLI reads TOML, applies a backend override, and requires an output path.
2. The facade resolves options, rejects conflicting reuse/resume, records
   configuration and source/dependency identity, and strips inherited `MHD_*`.
3. A fresh Julia child process activates the same project and thread count;
   backend extensions and transform plans are initialized there.
4. The driver initializes/imports/restores the state and advances MHD,
   photon response, chemistry, expansion, and gravity under the chosen controls.
5. Small diagnostics return histories/spectra; optional frames/checkpoints add
   larger host transfers. The parent records completion/failure and wall time.

Fresh-process isolation matters because the driver has compile-time constants
and backend caches. Running two `main()` calls after changing global environment
variables in one Julia session is not the supported orchestration API.
{{< src "scripts/run_pmf.jl" "function cli" >}}

## Independent analysis boundary {#sec-analysis-boundary}

The Python reference tools require NumPy, SciPy, and Matplotlib, not Julia or
GPU bindings. They implement their own linear/hierarchy evolution and consume
explicit data. Analysis scripts read production TSVs rather than requiring the
simulation to be loaded into memory. This separation is deliberate: independent
oracles can detect unit, clock, and phase errors hidden by same-code comparisons.

Not every inherited comparison tool consumes the facade's run directory
directly: some require upstream-style `manifest.json`, `summary.tsv`, a table,
or a controlled-linear-run contract. Read `tools/README.md` and each command's
help. Do not synthesize missing manifests to imply a nonlinear run passed a
linear-only validation gate.

`pmf-compare-nonlinear` is the native end-to-end entry point. It constructs the
handoff and resolved configuration, executes the standalone production process,
and consumes its real metadata and mode tables directly. Use that workflow
instead of adapting an inherited campaign manifest by hand.
